title: Reachability after a false input bit
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $l,l_1,l_0$ be program labels, let $st$ be a seven-register state, and let $c$ be an abstract configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$ calls the first oracle in whole-input mode with the input-pointer register as its sole argument, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and the bit of $x$ at position $st.P$, interpreted as false when that position is beyond the end of $x$, is false. If there is a finite run from label $l_0$ with registers initialized from $st$ to $c$, with every configuration before the endpoint satisfying the program guard and register bound $B$, then there is such a run from label $l$ to $c$.

replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $l,l_1,l_0$ program states, $st$ a
seven-register state, and $c$ a machine configuration. Suppose the instruction at $l$
calls the first oracle in whole-input mode with the input-pointer register as its sole
argument, every register of $st$ is at most $B$, and the bit of $x$ at position $st.P$
(taken to be false when that position is beyond the end of $x$) is false. If a bounded,
precondition-preserving run reaches $c$ from state $l_0$ with the registers initialized
from $st$, then such a run also reaches $c$ from state $l$ with those same initial
registers.
